title.narrative: Climate Change Supplementary Grant to Grant 2330484 (formerly GR002-01723-FLIS)

description.narrative: The main programme focuses on establishing agro-ecological methods and organic marketing. The climate funding enhances the existing project, extending its remit from increasing incomes, into making a comprehensive case for agro-ecological methods. This will increase enable farmers to make the case that this is also sound practice in adapting to climate change. While much of the growing methodology is sound practice in the face of climate change, the current project does not extend this more widely into testing and replicating additional climate change adaptation methods. Nor is it able to demonstrate the mitigation advantages of biodiverse cropping. The climate grant will allow both of these to happen. Training will be carried out with the existing cadre of farmers, to increase their skills around traditional beekeeping; pest management; and marketing produce. In order to encourage biodiversity (which has organic and adaptation advantages - but can lose out in the push to meet market demands) two much needed photovoltaic water pumps will be awarded as prizes to grower groups. Existing subsidies for "conventional" large scale chemical based agriculture can be regarded as a tax on small scale conservation organic agriculture. The project partners will make this case to government, along with raising the profile of organic produce. The government of Zimbabwe are open to this approach - already purchasing organically for hospitals and recommending it for people with HIV/AIDS. GardenAfrica has close links with Kew garden which is researching plants for pest control, and will now also be involved in looking at crops better suited to a changing climate. Discussions will be held with farmers to support thinking on how their methodologies enhance adaptation, with the best solutions widely disseminated.
